# id: # kind is false-positive or false-negative; status is open or closed.

description: Fixed by formal-mode-aware call scanning; covered by verification_diff_modular_call.adb.

Redundant_Boolean_Comparison fired on a same-named enumeration literal instead of Standard.True/False; fixed by requiring the non-literal operand's type to resolve to Standard.Boolean; covered by redundant_boolean_comparison_clean.adb.

Dead_Store, Overwritten_Assignment, and Repeated_Statement fired on Volatile/Atomic/Address-clause objects (memory-mapped hardware registers), where a write is observable on its own and does not need a later Ada-level read; fixed by an Is_Externally_Observable exemption in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow; covered by volatile_register_writes_clean.adb.

Global_Contract_Mismatch (and related Global/Depends/SPARK-readiness checks) fired on declarations with no SPARK_Mode aspect of their own nested inside a package/subprogram/task/protected body or spec marked SPARK_Mode => Off, because Effective_SPARK_Enabled only inspected the declaration itself and never walked up to the enclosing scope that the mode is inherited from; fixed by adding that lexical walk in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Dependency_Analysis, Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness, and Adalang_Analyzer.Flow_Interp; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, alarm-interfac.adb; covered by spark_mode_off_global_clean.adb.

Uninitialized_Output did not credit an out-mode parameter as initialized when the write happened inside a called nested subprogram whose own Global contract declares Output/In_Out mode on that variable as an up-level global, because Statement_Writes_Parameter only scanned actual parameters passed at the call site and never consulted the callee's own Global contract; fixed by adding Callee_Writes_Global in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, configdata.adb (ValidateFile / ReadLatchUnlock and siblings); covered by uninitialized_output_nested_call_clean.adb.

Depends_Contract_Mismatch, Incomplete_Depends_Contract, and Missing_Depends_Contract mishandled combined-output Depends syntax "(A, B) => C": Ada's own aggregate grammar has no comma-separated choice list (only "|" separates discrete choices), so Libadalang parses the parenthesized designator list as a nested positional aggregate rather than as separate identifier designators; every affected check only recognized a designator that was itself a plain identifier, so both outputs were silently dropped and the shared input was misreported as unused ("listed after null"); fixed by expanding the nested aggregate's own associations in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Dependency_Analysis.Parse_Depends and Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Collect_Depends_Outputs; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, configdata.adb (ReadDuration); covered by depends_combined_output_clean.adb.

Uninitialized_Output flagged composite (record- or array-typed) out parameters that were fully initialized field-by-field or element-by-element, because Same_Parameter only recognized a plain identifier as referring to the tracked parameter, not a selected component (Param.Field := ...) or an indexed/sliced name (Param (I) := ...); fixed by walking down through nested Dotted_Name and Call_Expr prefixes to the innermost identifier in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Same_Parameter; reproduced against AdaCore/spark2014 Tokeneer example, admin.adb (Logon), cert-attr-auth.adb and siblings (Extract); covered by uninitialized_output_composite_clean.adb. A remaining case (auditlog.adb, SetFileDetails) writes an array through a for-loop over its full index range rather than by literal index or field name; proving that covers every index would require reasoning about loop bounds matching the array's index subtype, a materially harder problem left open (see quality/external_corpus_findings.md).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter forwarded positionally to another overload of the same subprogram name, when several overloads shared the same parameter count and modes (a common shape for a family of Encode/Decode procedures differing only in one parameter's type): Call.P_Call_Params demands one fully precise overload resolution for the whole call and returns nothing when that fails, and the per-actual fallback Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) can itself raise in the same heavily-overloaded scenario; fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter by falling back, for a purely positional actual, to resolving only the callee name (a more lenient operation that still succeeds) and pairing by literal position via the new Callee_Formal_At_Position; reproduced against cubesatlab/cubedos, cubedos-lib-xdr.adb (the Encode family); covered by uninitialized_output_overloaded_forward_clean.adb. A distinct, narrower case remained open: a scalar written unconditionally inside a `for` loop with statically non-empty bounds and no early exit was still treated as possibly-unwritten, because every loop kind was conservatively assumed to be skippable; closed as FP-009.

Uninitialized_Output flagged a scalar out parameter written unconditionally inside a `for` loop with a statically non-empty range (e.g. `for I in 1 .. 3 loop ... Value := ...; end loop;`), because every loop kind was conservatively treated as possibly executing zero times; fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Interpret_Initialization by special-casing `for` loops: when the iteration range's bounds are statically known (via Adalang_Analyzer.Flow_Eval.Choice_Interval) and non-empty, and the loop body contains no exit/return/raise/goto anywhere (the new Contains_Loop_Escape), the body's own computed initialization result is trusted instead of discarded, since nothing can leave the loop before finishing a pass; while/plain loops and any `for` loop containing an early exit remain conservatively unresolved, to avoid trading this false positive for a false negative; found in cubedos-lib-xdr.adb's Encode family (the loop-based writes remaining after FP-008); verified with a fixture faithfully copying that loop shape rather than a fresh live re-run of the checkout; covered by uninitialized_output_static_loop_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_static_loop_early_exit.adb (still flags with an early exit present). This fix as originally landed introduced a false-negative regression on array parameters, because Same_Parameter's coarse whole-object treatment of "Arr (I) := ..." (see FP-007) let a write to just one index of a partial-range loop through the same trust condition; closed together with the array-loop-coverage case as FP-010 before any external report.

Following FP-009, a for-loop over a statically non-empty, escape-free range whose body wrote an array out-parameter through a single indexed write (e.g. `Arr (I) := ...;`) was trusted as fully initializing the whole array regardless of whether the loop's range actually covered every index, because Same_Parameter cannot distinguish "wrote one element" from "wrote every element"; caught by testing a 3-element array against a `for I in 1 .. 2 loop` before this shipped externally. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Interpret_Initialization by restricting the FP-009 trust path to non-array parameters and adding a separate, independent proof for arrays: the new Array_Index_Type resolves Param's own array-index subtype, Loop_Covers_Index_Range recognizes exactly two shapes whose iteration domain is provably that whole index range ("for I in Index_Type loop", a bare subtype mark naming the same index subtype, or "for I in Param'Range loop", whose coverage holds by construction independent of actual bounds), and List_Always_Writes_Loop_Index / Statement_Always_Writes_Loop_Index confirm the body unconditionally writes "Param (I)" indexed by exactly that control variable, recursing through if/case alternatives (an "if" with no "else" cannot be unconditional) the same way Interpret_Initialization's own Merge logic does; this also finally closes the FP-007-documented Tokeneer SetFileDetails case ("for I in LogFileIndexT loop LogFileEntries (I) := ...; end loop;") and the general array-loop-coverage limitation left open by FP-007/FP-009. An explicit "Low .. High" literal range that happens to match the array's bounds is deliberately left unrecognized (narrower in scope than the subtype-mark/'Range shapes, which need no bound arithmetic at all). Covered by uninitialized_output_array_loop_subtype_clean.adb and uninitialized_output_array_loop_range_attribute_clean.adb (clean), and uninitialized_output_array_loop_partial_range.adb and uninitialized_output_array_loop_range_attribute_early_exit.adb (still flag).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter written as "Subp_Name.Param := ...;" inside "procedure Subp_Name (Param : out ...)", where Subp_Name is the enclosing subprogram's own name used to qualify Param (Ada's general unit-name qualification, RM 8.3), typically to disambiguate from a same-named private component of an enclosing protected or task object that would otherwise shadow Param for simple-name visibility; Same_Parameter's prefix-unwrap loop always inspected the Dotted_Name's prefix ("Subp_Name") and discarded the suffix ("Param"), so it looked at the wrong identifier and concluded the parameter was never written. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Same_Parameter by checking, before the existing unwrap loop, whether the suffix matches Param's name and the prefix resolves to the new Enclosing_Subprogram_Or_Entry (the nearest enclosing Subp_Body or Entry_Body) -- a narrow, additive check that requires an exact match to the specific enclosing construct, so an unrelated same-named field access on a genuinely different parameter (e.g. "R.Size := ...;" where R is a different out/in-out parameter) is unaffected. Found via a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation run -P-less scan of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended): confirmed in aws-server-push.adb's protected body Waiter_Information (procedure Info, 4 parameters), Shutdown_If_Empty (Open), and Get (Queue) -- 6 of that file's 16 Uninitialized_Output findings, verified by diffing the exact same file's output before and after the fix. Covered by uninitialized_output_own_name_qualifier_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_own_name_qualifier_guard.adb (still flags the unrelated-object case).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter forwarded as a named actual (e.g. "Size => Size") to a protected operation whose formals include one typed Ada.Calendar.Time, because Libadalang's Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) fails to classify the actual at all in that shape (a formal typed Ada.Calendar.Time on an otherwise-unambiguous protected-operation call seems sufficient on its own to trip it; root cause is a Libadalang resolution limitation, not investigated further), and the FP-008 fallback (Callee_Formal_At_Position) only ever applied to purely positional actuals (Assoc.F_Designator = null), so a named actual hitting this gap had no fallback at all and was silently never recognized as a write. Fixed in Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter by adding the new Callee_Formal_By_Name (the named-actual counterpart to Callee_Formal_At_Position: same lenient callee-name-only resolution, matching by the designator's own name instead of by position) and using it whenever Assoc.F_Designator is not null. Found immediately after FP-011 in the very same aws-server-push.adb wrapper procedure "Info" (the outer, non-protected one forwarding to Waiter_Information.Info) while confirming that fix hadn't left a related gap open; reproduced with a minimal, non-generic 44-line fixture built by bisecting the real file (isolated to: a protected operation, 4 out-mode formals, one typed Ada.Calendar.Time, forwarded by named actual from an outer wrapper) after two closer, hand-written syntheses of the shape failed to reproduce it. A guard fixture confirms a named actual naming a genuinely "in" formal on a callee hitting the same resolution gap is not mistaken for writing an unrelated "out" parameter that is never forwarded. Covered by uninitialized_output_named_actual_forward_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_named_actual_forward_guard.adb (still flags the unrelated-parameter case).

Uninitialized_Output flagged an out parameter initialized solely via a parameterless prefixed procedure call (e.g. "Queue.Clear;", forwarding to Ada.Containers.Ordered_Maps.Clear), because such a call has no Call_Expr node -- Libadalang represents "Object.Operation;" as a bare Dotted_Name -- and Adalang_Analyzer.SPARK_Readiness.Statement_Writes_Parameter only ever inspected Ada_Call_Expr call statements, the same gap already fixed for Wrong_Parameter_Mode and Dead_Store in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Declarations.Parameter_Is_Written but left open here. Fixed in Statement_Writes_Parameter by adding an Ada_Dotted_Name branch that reuses Same_Parameter directly on the call node: its existing prefix-unwrap loop already reaches past the Dotted_Name's suffix (the method name) to the prefix, so no new unwrap logic was needed. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the residual Uninitialized_Output findings FP-011/FP-012 had left open in aws-server-push.adb: procedure Unregister_Clients's "Queue : out Tables.Map" is initialized only by "Queue.Clear;"; confirmed by diffing the file's own Uninitialized_Output output before and after the fix -- exactly that one finding disappeared, nothing new appeared, and the corpus-wide total dropped by exactly one. The other two residual Uninitialized_Output findings in the same file (Get_Data's "Data", Send's "Queue") were reviewed and are genuine: real paths (an empty chunk list; an early return before "Queue.Clear;") reach a normal return without ever writing the parameter, not analyzer mistakes. Covered by uninitialized_output_prefixed_clear_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_output_prefixed_clear_guard.adb (a second, unrelated out parameter left unwritten by the same call must still be flagged).

Wrong_Parameter_Mode recommended mode "out" for an in-out parameter written only through a selected component, indexed component, or slice of it (e.g. "State.Values (Index) := Value;"), because Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Declarations.Parameter_Is_Written's Assign_Stmt case delegated to Write_Target_Contains_Parameter, which deliberately unwraps any depth of nested selector/index to credit the base object as written -- correct for Dead_Store and Uninitialized_Output's coarser "was this touched at all" questions, but wrong for a mode-change recommendation: "out" formally disclaims any need for the incoming value, while a write to only part of a parameter inherently depends on every untouched part already holding a meaningful prior value. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's 126 Wrong_Parameter_Mode findings: 70 of them were AWS.Config.Set's single-field config setters (e.g. procedure Accept_Queue_Size, body "O.P (Accept_Queue_Size).Pos_Value := Value;"), each writing one element of Object's many-element parameter array while leaving every other configuration value untouched -- an in-out usage by construction, not a candidate for out. Fixed by adding Parameter_Is_Wholly_Written, identical to Parameter_Is_Written except its Assign_Stmt case requires the destination to be the parameter itself (Parameter_Name_Matches, no unwrap) rather than any nested selector/index reaching it, and using it (instead of the existing, still-unchanged Parameter_Is_Written) to gate only the "is only written; use mode out" recommendation in Analyze_Subprogram; the "is only read; use mode in" recommendation, Dead_Store, and Uninitialized_Output are unaffected. Confirmed against the real corpus: Wrong_Parameter_Mode findings dropped from 126 to 54 -- all 70 in aws-config-set.adb plus 2 more of the identical shape elsewhere (AWS.Net.Generic_Sets.Set_Data's "Set.Set (Index).Data := Data;", AWS.Client.HTTP_Utils.Decrement_Authentication_Attempt's "Counter (Level) := @ - 1;") -- with no new findings appearing anywhere. Covered by wrong_parameter_mode_partial_write_clean.adb (clean) and wrong_parameter_mode_partial_write_guard.adb (a direct, whole-object assignment must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a local scalar variable's own initializing assignment as a read of itself whenever the assignment's expression also mentioned an unrelated object's attribute of the same spelling (e.g. "Last := Fixed.Index (Data (First .. Data'Last), ...);", where the attribute designator "Last" in "Data'Last" has nothing to do with the local variable Last), because Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.Matches_Declaration -- shared read/write-detection infrastructure used by Uninitialized_Read, Dead_Store, and other data-flow checks -- falls back to a spelling-only comparison whenever semantic resolution fails, and Libadalang's own resolution correctly returns null for an attribute designator (it is syntactically an identifier but never refers to a declaration), which fed straight into that fallback. "First" and "Last" are two of the most common variable names for tracking string/array bounds, making this an easy, frequent collision with the identically-spelled standard attributes. Fixed by adding an early check in Matches_Declaration: an identifier that is specifically the F_Attribute child of its parent Attribute_Ref (not merely appearing somewhere inside one, so a genuine reference used as an attribute *prefix*, e.g. "Last'Size" where Last really is the tracked variable, is unaffected) never matches any declaration. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's Uninitialized_Read findings; reproduced with a minimal fixture before touching the fix, confirming the collision and that a differently-named variable does not trigger it. Confirmed against the real corpus: Uninitialized_Read findings dropped from 39 to 35 (aws-headers-values.adb, aws-log.adb, aws-config-ini.adb, aws-config-utils.adb, one each), with no new findings appearing anywhere and no change to any other check's totals in this corpus. Covered by uninitialized_read_attribute_designator_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_attribute_designator_guard.adb (a genuine attribute-prefix reference to the tracked variable must still be flagged).

Dead_Store flagged a write through an object-renaming declaration whose renamed object is part of a longer-lived parameter or global (e.g. "Info : Error_Details renames Self.Error_Detail;" where Self is an in-out parameter, then "Info := Some_Error;") as a dead store whenever "Info" itself was never read again by name within the same subprogram, even though the write is really to Self.Error_Detail -- observable by the caller after return and by any other code that later reads Self.Error_Detail directly. Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Control_Flow.Is_Local_To_Subprogram, the lexical-scope test Dead_Store uses to decide whether a written declaration is purely local, considers a renaming declaration "local" whenever it is textually nested inside the subprogram, regardless of what it aliases; and Data_Flow.Ultimate_Object (used by Assigned_Declaration to resolve a bare "Info := ...;" target) only follows a renamed object that is itself a bare identifier ("Y renames X;"), not one reached through a selected component, indexed component, or dereference, so it never unwound "Self.Error_Detail" back to Self's own (non-local, non-Object_Decl) declaration. Fixed by adding Renames_Nonlocal_Object in Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Control_Flow: walks the renamed object down through any depth of selected/indexed component or dereference (the same coarse, whichever-depth-only-the-base-object-matters treatment already used elsewhere in this project, e.g. Same_Parameter) to its base identifier, and disqualifies Decl from Dead_Store whenever that base is not itself local to Subprogram. A renaming of a genuinely local object's field is unaffected. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the corpus's Dead_Store findings: 13 of the 23 were concentrated in a single file, aws-http2-stream.adb, all of this exact shape. Confirmed against the real corpus: Dead_Store findings dropped from 23 to 10, all 13 in aws-http2-stream.adb, with no new findings appearing anywhere. Covered by dead_store_renaming_of_parameter_field_clean.adb (clean) and dead_store_renaming_of_parameter_field_guard.adb (a renaming of a genuinely local object's field must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable's read inside a nested subprogram or entry body as happening before that variable's genuine initializing write elsewhere in the enclosing subprogram, whenever the nested body's own declaration was textually positioned earlier than the write, even though the nested body is only actually invoked (and its read only actually reached) after that write runs. Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.First_Access is a plain pre-order AST walk with no notion of actual call order: a nested subprogram body is a declaration, elaborated but not executed at its own textual position, yet the walk recursed into it exactly like any other statement, discovering a read inside it before ever reaching a later statement of the enclosing subprogram that writes the same variable. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the 5 Uninitialized_Read findings FP-015 had left open in aws-headers-values.adb: Split's nested function To_Set calls Next_Value (whose out-mode formals initialize To_Set's own locals Name_First, Name_Last, Value_First, Value_Last) before ever invoking its own nested function Element, which reads those locals as up-level references; Element's declaration, though, textually precedes that Next_Value call. The same shape affected Split itself over First (read inside To_Set, textually preceding Split's own initializing assignment to First). Fixed by skipping recursion into a child node of kind Ada_Subp_Body or Ada_Entry_Body during First_Access's walk; this trades away detecting a genuine read through a nested body invoked before the tracked variable's initialization (unrecognized, not soundly ruled out) for not flagging the common, correct case, consistent with this project's general bias toward fewer false positives. Confirmed against the real corpus: Uninitialized_Read findings dropped from 35 (the count after FP-015/FP-016) to 29 -- 7 instances across aws-net-acceptors.adb, aws-url-set.adb, and aws-headers-values.adb disappeared, and one previously-hidden, separate finding in aws-net-acceptors.adb (a different variable, unrelated root cause) was exposed by no longer stopping the scan early -- see the "still open" note in external_corpus_findings.md. Covered by uninitialized_read_nested_subprogram_order_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_nested_subprogram_order_guard.adb (a genuine direct read in the enclosing subprogram's own statements, near an unrelated nested subprogram, must still be flagged).

Uninitialized_Read flagged a scalar local variable as read before assignment even when it was genuinely initialized by being forwarded (positionally or by name) as an out/in-out actual to a callee whose per-actual resolution Libadalang's own Assoc.P_Get_Params (Imprecise_Fallback => True) fails to classify -- the same resolution fragility already fixed for Uninitialized_Output's write detection in FP-008/FP-012 (a formal typed Ada.Calendar.Time on an otherwise-unambiguous call is one confirmed trigger; heavy overload is another), but Adalang_Analyzer.Checks.Data_Flow.Call_Writes_Declaration and Call_Reads_Simple_Actual -- the corresponding read/write detection Uninitialized_Read's First_Access uses -- had no equivalent fallback: when P_Get_Params found nothing, the actual was silently treated as neither read nor written, and the scan continued past the real initializing call to whatever came next, misreporting that as the first access. Fixed by adding Callee_Formal_At_Position, Callee_Formal_By_Name, and Formal_Mode to Checks.Data_Flow (duplicating, not sharing, the equivalent functions already in SPARK_Readiness, consistent with this project's existing per-module-helper style) and using them, exactly as Statement_Writes_Parameter already does, whenever P_Get_Params resolves no formal at all for a given actual. Found in a fresh AWS (Ada Web Server, AdaCore/aws) validation re-run of src/core, src/extended, src/http2 (273 files, --recommended) while investigating the aws-net-acceptors.adb finding FP-017 had exposed: confirmed, in isolation, that the same Ada.Calendar.Time-formal trigger already known from FP-012 also breaks Call_Writes_Declaration (reproduced with a minimal fixture derived from the FP-012 shape before touching the fix). Confirmed against the real corpus: one instance disappeared, aws-session.adb's Get_Value (Found, forwarded positionally to Get_Node). The aws-net-acceptors.adb finding that motivated this investigation, however, remains: it reproduces only in the full 273-file batch context, not standalone, and even Callee_Formal_At_Position's own callee-name resolution (Call.F_Name.P_Referenced_Decl) apparently fails in that deeper context, a different and unresolved layer of the same general problem, left open. Covered by uninitialized_read_positional_forward_clean.adb (clean) and uninitialized_read_positional_forward_guard.adb (a variable never forwarded at all, at the same resolution-fragile callee shape, must still be flagged).
